paras: The killing of Patton and Mallory took place at Independence, a mining camp about twenty miles west of Leadville, Colorado, shortly after dark on or about December 16, 1881, when townspeople chased down and shot two men described as desperadoes. The pair had been firing revolvers in the streets, and a crowd 'riddled' them with bullets, after which a vigilance committee formed to hang others of their kind, who fled. A single Leadville dispatch carried the story across the country, where papers headlined it as summary justice.

According to a Leadville special to the Denver Tribune, Independence had 'for a long time been overrun with desperate characters' who kept the camp in 'a perpetual state of turmoil'. The dispatch said bands of these men would take possession of the camp, shoot men down in the streets and force stores to close for hours at a time. It described Patton and Mallory as two such men, 'having the repution of killing a number of men'.

Shortly after dark, the two, said to be drunk, started up the streets firing revolvers 'promiscuously'; one rewrite said they fired 'among the people'. The townspeople 'turned out en masse' and pursued them until they were 'brought to bay and literally riddled with bullets'. The two returned the fire 'of the mob, but without effect'. No account states in so many words that they died, though the St. Paul Daily Globe headlined the item 'Desperadoes Killed With Bullets'.

A little later a vigilance committee was formed 'for the purpose of hanging three or four of the worst blacklegs', but nearly all of that class left town at once. Weekly digests described the exodus as 'a hegira of bad characters'. No report of an inquest, arrest or any official action appears in the coverage, and no paper gave the race of the dead men.

The story reached readers almost entirely through the Tribune's Leadville special, which the Cheyenne Daily Leader printed on December 18 under the headline 'A Law Unto Themselves'. Over the following days it ran in St. Paul, Portland, Salt Lake City, Memphis and Chicago, under headlines such as 'Desperadoes Summarily Dealt With' and 'Town Cleansed of Blackleg'. The Somerset Herald was still running it on December 28 as 'Summary Punishment of Desperadoes'.

Shorter versions appeared in news digests, often next to reports of the cowboy riot at Caldwell, Kansas, and presented the townspeople as citizens or miners clearing out bad men. No paper criticized the shooting, and the wire's opening account of a terrorized camp served as its justification. No Black-press coverage exists for this period.

The earliest dispatch, dated December 17, put the shooting 'last night', and the Sacramento Daily Record-Union said 'Friday night', both pointing to December 16, while one rewritten account said 'Saturday night'. The names also varied in transmission, appearing as Patton or Patten and Mallory, Malloy or Malery, and in one digest as 'Mallory and Pallen', a form that matches the Chicago Tribune's closing misprint 'Pullen and Mallory'.

bases: Townspeople 'en masse' pursued two men who had been firing revolvers in the streets and 'riddled' them with bullets, and a vigilance committee then formed to hang others, an act headlined as summary punishment (A1, A2, A20).

No account states outright that the men died, but they were 'literally riddled with bullets' and one headline reads 'Desperadoes Killed With Bullets' (A1, A2); the killers were 'the people' or 'citizens' acting without legal authority, and the papers framed it as summary punishment of men who had a reputation for killing (A1, A4, A20). The two were themselves firing and returned the mob's fire, so the killing was part of an armed chase as much as an execution (A1, A7).
Every account traces to one Leadville special to the Denver Tribune, reprinted and condensed (A1, A2, A7); no local, independent or follow-up report was found.

accounts.label: Leadville special to the Denver Tribune
accounts.gist: Independence had long been terrorized by desperadoes; Patton and Mallory, drunk, fired revolvers in the streets, were chased down and riddled by the people, and a vigilance committee then drove out the remaining 'blacklegs'.

accounts.label: Rewritten account
accounts.gist: Places the shooting on Saturday night and calls the shooters 'an exasperated mob'; the committee was organized 'to lynch a few others of the gang'.

accounts.label: News digests
accounts.gist: One-sentence items say the two were riddled with bullets by citizens or miners after causing trouble, followed by a 'hegira of bad characters'.

framing.detail: Headlines such as 'Desperadoes Summarily Dealt With' and 'Town Cleansed of Blackleg' and the wire's account of a camp in 'perpetual state of turmoil' presented the shooting as a deserved clean-up.
Most papers ran the Tribune special or a one-line digest of it without comment, often in crime columns next to the Caldwell, Kansas, cowboy riot.
